runs.prompt: Does the EU AI Act ban facial recognition in public places? Explain the actual rule and cite two real sources. Prefer an official EU source.
runs.answer:
**Short answer:** Yes, but only for a specific category. The EU AI Act prohibits **real-time remote biometric identification (RBI)**—live facial recognition that identifies people as they move through publicly accessible spaces—when used for **law enforcement**. It is not a blanket ban on every camera or every private use of facial recognition in public.

**The actual rule**

- **Article 5(1)(h)** bans real-time RBI in publicly accessible spaces for law-enforcement purposes [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/what-systems-are-prohibited-under-article-5-ai-act-eg-social-scoring-emotion-recognition).
- The prohibition is not absolute. Under **Article 5(1)(h)(i)–(iii)**, it may be set aside only when strictly necessary for narrow objectives such as the targeted search for specific victims of crime (including missing children), the prevention of a specific, substantial and imminent threat to life or physical safety or of a terrorist attack, and the detection or prosecution of perpetrators of serious crimes [Guidance Study, Publications Office of the EU](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/24b979fc-4829-11f1-8095-01aa75ed71a1/language-en).
- **Article 5(2)** imposes procedural safeguards, including prior authorisation by a judicial or independent administrative authority and a documented procedural record before any exception is used [Guidance Study, Publications Office of the EU](https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/24b979fc-4829-11f1-8095-01aa75ed71a1/language-en).

**Scope and limits**

- Police cannot run live facial-recognition scanning of crowds in streets, stations or parks as general surveillance.
- Uses outside law enforcement (for example, retail, stadiums or office access control) are not covered by this prohibition, though many fall under separate high-risk obligations in Annex III [AI Act Service Desk – Biometrics](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/biometrics).
- The rule concerns **real-time** identification; retrospective analysis of footage is treated differently under the Act.

**Bottom line:** The EU AI Act bans live, police-operated facial recognition in publicly accessible spaces, subject to tightly controlled exceptions and prior authorisation. It does not ban all facial recognition in public places.

runs.prompt: What changed in the latest iPhone compared with the previous model? Give three changes that matter and cite one hands-on review.
runs.answer:
**iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max vs. iPhone 17 Pro / Pro Max**

1. **Variable-aperture main camera** — the main lens can switch apertures, giving more flexibility across lighting conditions and depth control than the 17 Pro’s fixed lens [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/tech/986400/apple-iphone-18-pro-max-hands-on-impressions-september-2026-event).
2. **New “pro” camera controls** — added manual controls give photographers more shooting options [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/tech/986400/apple-iphone-18-pro-max-hands-on-impressions-september-2026-event).
3. **Color-matched glass back** — the rear glass blends more seamlessly with the aluminum frame, replacing the previous two-tone look [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/tech/986400/apple-iphone-18-pro-max-hands-on-impressions-september-2026-event).
